packageRules.description: @n8n/node-cli lands by hand. Two independent reasons, either one sufficient. (1) It EMITS the published tarball, and the artifact-tool law exact-pins every such tool because two installs on different days must not build different bytes — a tool that assembles the artifact should not land unattended. (2) It CARRIES @n8n/eslint-plugin-community-nodes, which is the ruleset n8n Cloud verification is judged against — an external contract that changes without asking us. A bump is a contract change to read, not a dependency to absorb. Found the expensive way: the pin sat 21 versions back, freezing that ruleset at 56 of its current 176 rules while `pnpm lint:n8n` stayed green.
